manifest.title: fun-lab: the broadcast payloads of xp.awarded, metric.level-reached, achievement.unlocked and prize.awarded

contract.summary: A scenario, as in fun-lab/progression, but what is pinned is the WIRE payload of each broadcastable event: exactly what laravel-fun-lab's broadcastWith() returns, the JSON a Laravel Echo listener receives and @particle-academy/fancy-fun-lab-ui reads (feedItemFromEcho, FunLabXpFeed, FunLabLevelUp). A twin emits its own in-process event object; its payload serializer must turn that object into this document, key for key and type for type. The channel name is not pinned: PHP derives it from the awardable's class name, which a twin has none of.

functions.broadcasts: broadcasts(input: {clock, config?, subjects, steps}) -> {steps: [{result, broadcasts: [{event, payload}]}]}. Steps and results are those of fun-lab/progression's scenario(). broadcasts lists, in emission order, every xp.awarded, metric.level-reached, achievement.unlocked and prize.awarded event the step emitted, each with its broadcastWith() payload. award.granted and catalog.mutated do not broadcast and are not listed.

contract.referenceNote: Goldens are laravel-fun-lab's own event classes: tests/Conformance/ScenarioRunner.php listens for each event and records $event->broadcastWith(), at the frozen clock, and tests/Conformance/ExportFixturesTest.php writes the table. Inputs are authored in fancy-conformance/scripts/fun-lab/events.input.json.

manifest.notes: Added because the twins' 0.1.0 events carried raw rows ({profile, profileMetric, metric, ...}) while laravel-fun-lab broadcasts flat payloads, and the UI rendered "+5 XP in {metric}" against a twin. fun-lab/progression pinned which events fire and in what order, never their payloads, so nothing failed. No discrimination probes, as for the other fun-lab suites.

cases.title: xp.awarded carries the flat payload: ids, the metric's slug and name, the amount, the metric's new total and level, reason, source and occurred_at
cases.notes: The UI's feed reads gamed_metric_name. A raw event with the name nested under metric renders the label with its {metric} placeholder unfilled.

cases.title: reason and source are present and null when the award gave none, and the metric's name defaults from its slug
cases.notes: A key that is absent and a key that is null are different JSON; a twin that drops a null key fails here.

cases.title: an award crossing two levels broadcasts each level, ascending, with what it granted, then the achievements, then xp.awarded at the final level
cases.notes: achievements is a list of {id, slug, name, icon}, icon null when unset, and lists only what that level granted. total_xp on each level is the metric's XP when the level was reached.

cases.title: a level whose achievement the profile already holds broadcasts achievements as an empty list, and an unnamed level is called Level 2
cases.notes: An empty list, never an empty object and never absent. level_name is the level's stored name, which setup defaults to 'Level N'.

cases.title: xp.awarded's id is the profile's row for that metric: the same on every award to it, different per profile and per metric
cases.notes: Catches an id taken from the event log row or a per-event counter: those would differ on the fourth award, where the profile-metric id repeats the first.

cases.title: with the event log off the payloads are unchanged, id included
cases.notes: The payload does not read the event log, so turning it off changes nothing on the wire.

cases.title: achievement.unlocked and prize.awarded carry the grant payloads: grant id, profile, the item's slug and name, status for a prize, and granted_at
cases.notes: The second first-login grant is refused and broadcasts nothing. granted_at follows the clock.

cases.title: occurred_at is the time of the award, in Carbon's toIso8601String form
cases.notes: +00:00, not Z, and no fractional seconds.
